value.rationale: Sixteen-point biplanes form a classical three-isomorphism-type design testbed; the natural identification problem is to distinguish all blocks by as few observed points as possible. The proof yields the complete optimal class (all and only 96 block punctures) uniformly across all designs, with a two-type exact graph code classification for the five-regular Clebsch graph. The precise count and structural mechanism are not merely the standard 16-block incidence table or general information bound, and inform optimal sensor placements.
